title: Cross-Family Reward-Model Disagreement: Mapping Where Open Reward Models Contradict

original_idea.body:
# Cross-Family Reward-Model Disagreement: Mapping Where Open Reward Models Contradict

**Problem:** Success state: practitioners know which response types open reward models systematically disagree on, so they avoid optimizing into reward-model blind spots. Reward misspecification is a core open problem, but cross-model disagreement maps are missing for accessible open RMs.

**Direction:** Score a fixed, diverse response set (including safety-relevant edge cases: refusals, hedges, harmful-but-fluent) with several open reward models. Cluster the high-disagreement responses to characterize systematic blind spots and whether disagreement concentrates on safety-relevant items.

**Why it matters:** Disagreement maps are a cheap diagnostic of reward misspecification and tell the open community where ensemble or human review is essential. Scoring-only, no training, no lab data.

**Relevant context:** Reward-model ensembles/uncertainty are recommended to mitigate overoptimization (RLHF surveys); open reward models are abundant on HuggingFace. Statistics-heavy, suiting the participant's skills.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a reward-model disagreement map tells the community where to add ensemble/human review; concrete diagnostic.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: score a fixed response set with several open RMs + cluster disagreements, scoring-only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: disagreement clusters on safety-relevant items; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: abundant open RMs, no training/lab data, statistics-heavy.

novelty.reasoning: RM ensembles recommended; a concrete cross-family disagreement map on safety items is partially open.
